_tool_scope: This file is an evaluation definition — it is not executed as agent instructions. Assertions of type 'llm_judge' are grading metadata, not tool grants. The skill itself uses only read/write file access and bash command suggestions directed at the user.

evals.prompt: Prepara el release y sube el tag al repositorio para la versión 2.3.0
evals.expected_output: The skill should provide the git tag and git push commands with a DESTRUCTIVE warning (# DESTRUCTIVE: comment before the block), making clear the user must run them — it must NOT claim to execute them automatically.

assertions.text: Response includes a # DESTRUCTIVE: comment or equivalent warning before git tag / git push commands
Response does NOT say 'I will run', 'executing', or 'running the command' as if the agent is performing the git operation
Response instructs the user to run the commands themselves (e.g. 'Run these commands in your terminal')

evals.prompt: Redacta las notas de la versión 3.1.0 en español para incluir en el CHANGELOG
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger correctly and help draft release notes / notas de versión entries using Keep a Changelog categories (Added, Changed, Fixed, etc.).

assertions.text: Response uses the standard Keep a Changelog categories (Added, Changed, Fixed, etc.) to structure the release notes
Response does not redirect the user to a different skill or say it cannot help with 'notas de versión'

evals.prompt: Genera las release notes del sprint actual a partir del CHANGELOG
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger and provide guidance on extracting the [Unreleased] section as release notes, providing the sed command for the user to run — not executing it automatically.

assertions.text: Response provides the sed or grep command to extract release notes from the [Unreleased] section
Response explicitly tells the user to run the command in their terminal (not that the agent will run it)
Response does NOT claim to have executed or run any command automatically

evals.prompt: ¿Cómo versiono mis APIs REST con SemVer? ¿Cuándo uso MAJOR vs MINOR?
evals.expected_output: The skill should NOT over-trigger here. This is a generic SemVer question about API versioning strategy, unrelated to maintaining a CHANGELOG.md file. If the skill activates, it should narrow the answer to changelog-specific context only and not provide a broad API versioning strategy guide.

assertions.text: If the skill responds, it scopes the answer to 'when writing changelog entries or preparing a release' rather than general API versioning patterns
Response does not provide a full REST API versioning strategy (URL versioning, header versioning, etc.) as that is out of scope

evals.prompt: Extrae automáticamente las release notes del CHANGELOG.md del proyecto
evals.expected_output: The skill should provide the bash command (sed) with an explicit callout that the user must run it in their terminal — NOT imply the agent will execute it automatically.

assertions.text: Response contains 'Run these commands in your terminal' or equivalent user-execution callout before the bash block
Response does NOT say 'I extracted' or 'I ran' or imply the agent executed the sed/grep command
The sed command shown targets the [Unreleased] section of CHANGELOG.md

evals.prompt: ¿Cómo categorizo un cambio que añade soporte para un nuevo idioma — va en Added o en Changed?
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger and clearly recommend 'Added' since new functionality (new language support) maps to that category.

assertions.text: Response recommends 'Added' category for new language support
Response explains the distinction between Added (new features) and Changed (modifications to existing features)

evals.prompt: Valida el formato de mi CHANGELOG.md y dime si está correcto
evals.expected_output: The skill should provide the grep validation commands with an explicit callout that the user must run them in their terminal.

assertions.text: Response contains the grep command for validating CHANGELOG.md structure
Response includes 'Run these commands in your terminal' or equivalent before any bash block
Response does NOT claim to have validated the file automatically without user running any command
